chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is a Garden which none enter except for three: a man who ruled against himself with the truth, and a man who visited his believing brother for the sake of Allah, and a man who preferred his believing brother for the sake of Allah.
ai.seo_question: What are the three types of people who will enter Paradise according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), linking the spiritual hierarchy of Paradise to three distinct acts of piety: self-discipline, social connection, and altruism. This triad reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing individual moral accountability (muhasabah) with communal solidarity (ukhuwwah), illustrating that true faith manifests in both internal rectitude and external generosity towards fellow believers.
